text:
If you’re heading onto the lake, the Lake Wind Advisory is the headline today: south winds will flip northwest at 15 to 25 knots, with waves building to 3 to 5 feet before easing. Around Burlington, a strong front is bringing a few showers this morning, and a secondary boundary keeps a stray shower possible into the afternoon. The clouds should break some, but it’ll stay raw and gusty, with a high right around 58 and northwest gusts up to 32 mph. The models are split on how many showers develop, so I’d keep the rain jacket handy even if the dry stretches win out.

Tonight turns partly cloudy, breezy, and colder, with a low around 39. Tuesday is the cleaner day, sunny with a high near 55, though a stiff northwest breeze remains. The lake settles to 1 to 3-foot waves, but the water is only 61, so plan on a short, sheltered outing Tuesday, not a long open-water trip.
